doc.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Learning to build on chord symbols
summary: Wall says hearing Wes made him want to do something creative with a chord symbol.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: When did you first hit on the concept of looking at a chord symbol and building something from it?
Well just the difference of actually having to play written out music.

Immediately. I think because, well I say immediately not in the very beginning of listening to the Stones. When I heard that I heard guitar parts from records and I saw chord symbols. But when I heard Wes play for instance, and I heard what was happening, you know I heard lines happening, there was something more happening over this harmonic bass, that’s when I wanted to do something with the chord symbol. That’s when I realized you could do something creative with this, with this foundation here, and I think that’s when that whole process started. And I’m still trying to find out what to do with all this.
